### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-email`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-loader.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fe1249b70292e4e8ba3188ddbbf96383d5400087`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-loader.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **54** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fe1249b70292e4e8ba3188ddbbf96383d5400087` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8e1bbdd79dac27b4b78566e7ac317455d52fdcfd` — the merge of head `a52f89e003f115ba5691c5105bd26371b9c1bcfa` into base `fe1249b70292e4e8ba3188ddbbf96383d5400087`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8e1bbdd79dac27b4b78566e7ac317455d52fdcfd && git checkout 8e1bbdd79dac27b4b78566e7ac317455d52fdcfd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fe1249b70292e4e8ba3188ddbbf96383d5400087 a52f89e003f115ba5691c5105bd26371b9c1bcfa && git checkout -B drift-repro fe1249b70292e4e8ba3188ddbbf96383d5400087 && git merge --no-ff a52f89e003f115ba5691c5105bd26371b9c1bcfa

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fe1249b70292e4e8ba3188ddbbf96383d5400087
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fe1249b70292e4e8ba3188ddbbf96383d5400087` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The bundled-type keep (`ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` only) serves a member of a customization pair of X, or of a holder that X admitted, as the layers reached it (ADR-0146, #28390 ruling A). Every other type keeps its replacement.

- **Red line 3: holds.** Q2 (the `auth.*` platform names stay at one holder per deployment) and Q4 (a bundle addition still meets its holder) are as read on the card.

Q3's two conditions (no second subscription across the upgrade, and fail-closed in a mixed-version window) apply to the webhook PR, not this one.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a52f89e003f115ba5691c5105bd26371b9c1bcfa`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-read.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-e8-readers.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-bare-name-one-holder-ai-family.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-bare-name-one-holder-flow-family.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-loader.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-loader.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/bare-name-one-holder-flow-family.dogfood.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/stored-references.integration.test.ts + read, never reviewed: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-write-gates.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-overlay-merge.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-environment-rows.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/customization-pair-lookup.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/io-node-config.zod.ts, docs/adr/0150-behavioural-metadata-addressed-by-package-objects-keep-the-literal-prefix.md (main fe1249b7), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ResourceListPage.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ResourceEditPage.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioBundleItemEditor.tsx

Inputs: card #31699 (body and its 6 comments), PR #32089 (body, 17 files, net diff against main fe1249b7, which is the merge base), the check-runs on the head. Everything below was read in the tree, nothing was run.

Check-runs on the head when read: every completed run is `success` or `skipped` (Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, the Lint family, Type Check source gates and debt ledger, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI). Still `in_progress`: Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16, Type Check workspace, Type Check consumer gates, Type Check UI, Build and E2E UI. Those gate verdicts do not exist yet; this record does not stand in for them.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `NAMESPACE_SCOPED_BARE_NAME_TYPES` gains `email_template`. The package door (`installPackage`), the item seam (`registerItem`) and the cold-boot seal (`sealBareNameHolders`) accept a second package holder of another namespace. Implemented as declared: `bareNameHoldersMeet` still answers true for a co-owner, a package with no namespace, and base/system/sys (through the caller's namespace reading), and built-ins are still added by `bareNameHoldersOtherThan`. RIGHT as an accept-set change; whether the type was ready for it is F1 in ④.
2. `bareNameHoldersMeet` gains an optional fourth parameter `name`; a platform-requested name keeps one holder. All three call sites pass it (door, seam, seal). Additive. RIGHT.
3. `PLATFORM_REQUESTED_BARE_NAMES_BY_TYPE.email_template`: eight names. Census by reading: the eight `auth.*` literals in plugin-auth and plugin-email are exactly the eight listed; no other package under `packages/` sends a template by a literal name. The resolver now answers them environment-wide for a package caller too (`via: unique-holder`, not `closure`), which the two forced test edits state. RIGHT, and it follows seat ruling Q2 = A and the epic read.
4. New exports `declaredBundleMembers`, `BundleHolding`, `isBundleAdditionPair`; `registeredBundleHolding`, `bareNameBundleAdditionMeets`, `declaredBundleHolding` private to the registry. The addition test is the same three conditions as the registry's existing `isBundleAddition` (reach, no reach back, no common member). A bundle addition of another namespace is still refused naming its base at the door, the seam and the seal. RIGHT, and it follows Q4 = A.
5. `PACKAGE_SCOPED_READ_TYPES` gains `email_template`: the bare `/meta/email_template/NAME` read goes through the resolver (two holders answer 409 naming both), and `?package=` and `/meta/email_template/NS/NAME` take G1's exact qualifier. RIGHT as wired. The exact-qualifier refusal is declared. The bare read's 409 for a clash sealed before phase 1 is a narrowing ADR-0150's covered-types paragraph asks each row that meets it to declare; the PR's lines do not name it (N1).
6. `ExactQualifierRegistry.packageScopedHoldersOf` takes the named package as caller; `exactQualifierItem` keeps a pair-stamped item for `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` types. Judged in ④.
7. `template-loader.ts`: comment only, no code. The send still resolves with no caller. RIGHT as a description of the code; its consequence is F1.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/31699-email-template-names-per-namespace.md`: objectql minor, core minor, metadata-protocol patch, plugin-email patch; a `!` subject; a BREAKING paragraph with the one-line fix; one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`); both declaration lines present and equal to the PR body's.

- `Metadata-protocol: added` (a name a second namespace's package may now declare) takes at least minor on a package the diff moves: objectql and core are minor. Matches. Check Changeset is `success` on the head.
- Clause-②: yes (narrowing) is the right arm for what the diff narrows: a by-name email template read naming a package that holds no item of the name was served and is now refused. The `!` and the BREAKING paragraph match that. The ADR-0087 disposition is right: no key, value or stored row changes shape.
- The changeset's sentence "So a package no longer has to rename an email template because a package of another namespace already ships one of that name" overstates what the head delivers: see F1. If F1 is ruled as accepted behaviour, this sentence and the BREAKING paragraph must say that every send of a two-holder name is refused.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report `status: rework`, `open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none`, `out_of_scope_findings: []`. Nothing to answer there.
- Deviation 1 (stored-references measured on `--dev` databases of app-crm and app-showcase, all empty): accepted; the seat order asked for those two apps.
- Deviation 2 (the co-owner dogfood asserts 403 `NOT_OVERRIDABLE`; the bare-name 422 for a co-owner is pinned in objectql only): accepted; the registry test carries the rule's own refusal.
- Deviation 3 (the exact-qualifier change in metadata-protocol, outside the card's named surface): judged in ④; the two changes themselves hold, with F2.
- `dogfood_battery: n/a — no ! in the PR title and no (narrowing) arm` is stale on this head: the title now carries `!` and the arm is `(narrowing)`. The PR body says the full battery on `a52f89e0` is still running. ESCALATED to the seat: the battery result is owed before landing.
- The card's acceptance says a narrowing beyond the declared one goes to the maintainer before landing. The card declares `Clause-②: no` and a narrowing for co-owners only; the claim and the epic carry-in say `Narrowing: no`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. The PR declares `yes (narrowing)` for the exact qualifier on a new type. Whether G1's ruling on #31691 already covers each type that joins the readers is not readable from this review's inputs. ESCALATED to the seat and the epic seat: name the ruling, or file `needs-user-decision`.
- F1 below is a second effect beyond the declared narrowing, and falls under the same acceptance line.

### ④ Design judgment

**F1 — must-fix. The narrowing admits a state in which no send of the name works, and the send has no qualified address.**

- `SendTemplateInput` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.ts`) names no package, and the flow notify node sends through `IEmailService.sendTemplate({ template, locale })` (`io-node-config.zod.ts`). The loader resolves every send as a caller with no package (`readBundle` in `template-loader.ts`: `resolvePackageScopedName(scoped, { type, name })`, no caller) and throws `EmailTemplateAmbiguousError` when two packages hold the name.
- On base, a second namespace's package that ships a held template name was refused at install (422), and the first package's sends kept working. On this head the install succeeds with no warning, and from then on every send of that name, from the first package's flows as from the second's, fails 409. The dogfood pins exactly this ("install-local of a third namespace's package shipping the held template name installs", "a send of the template two namespaces ship is refused with 409").
- Against the published record on `main`: ADR-0150 D9 narrows a type "only after that type's indexes, doors and stored references all carry the package"; D3 says a reference written inside package P is a bare name resolved from P; D10 says a second package installed later "does not change what any stored reference, overlay, run or URL of the first one means. That is the guarantee this whole record buys." The send door carries no package, a package flow's `template:` reference is not resolved from its package, and the second install changes what the first package's reference means: from its template to a refusal. The epic carry-in on the card asks the same thing ("Every reader of the type resolves by ADR-0150 D3 (package, name), and the G1 qualified addresses reach each holder"): `/meta` has a qualified address, the send has none.
- The diff states the reason itself, for eight names only: `bare-name-one-holder.ts` keeps the `auth.*` names at one holder because "its requester can name no package, so two holders would leave it refused as ambiguous on every request". Every requester of a send is in that position today.
- This is a capability declared (two namespaces each ship the name) and not delivered at its consumer (neither can be sent), bought by taking a working send away from the first holder at runtime. Dispositions, either one: (a) the send carries the caller's package (the flow or hook that sends, resolved by D3 from P) before `email_template` joins `NAMESPACE_SCOPED_BARE_NAME_TYPES`, which is the E5 half this type still owes; or (b) a maintainer ruling (`needs-user-decision`, the card's own acceptance line) that accepts the send's refusal as an exception to D10, declared in the changeset and the PR body as what an operator sees and how to recover. The readers and the exact qualifier in this PR can land without the switch.

**F2 — should-fix. Two newly reachable states where `?package=ID` does not serve "that package's own", unpinned.** Read, not run.

- Sibling members of one App. X and Y both depend on App A, declare different namespaces, and each ships `welcome` en-US; the head admits both (neither is an addition to the other). `pairsOf(X)` and `pairsOf(Y)` are both A's pair (`appOf`). A locale added in Studio lands as one row in A's pair with no `overrides` declaration; `findPairAddedMemberRow` reads it for either base, and the new keep in `exactQualifierItem` (`isPairOf(served, base)`) serves it on both `?package=X` and `?package=Y`. Without the keep it was served only where the pair is no registered package. The row cannot say whose template it adds to.
- A legacy package-less row. `servedOverlayRowCandidates` tries the package-less row after the named package's own; `withRowBinding` leaves it unstamped and `exactQualifierItem` passes an unstamped item through. A package-less row written as the one holder's overlay is, once a second namespace holds the name, served on both holders' exact addresses, while the registry (`overlaySlotBinding`) binds it to neither. This part is the row layer's ADR-0048 fallback, on `main` for the nine other types; the narrowing makes it reachable for an email template.
- Fix: pin each state with the answer the epic seat rules for it (serve, or refuse naming both), or state both in the changeset beside "serve that package's own" and carry them on a follow-up card.

**The exact-qualifier deviation, as asked.**

- Change 1 (the holder ask passes the named package as caller): holds. `packageScopedHoldersOf` reads the caller in one place, the filter `id === callerPackageId || !isBundleAddition(id)`, so the only package the caller can add to the answer is itself, and only when it already holds a member. A package that holds nothing of the name is still refused, and the refusal's candidates still leave out another package's addition. An admitted addition reads its own members only: `getPackageScopedItem` and `pickBundleMember` answer nothing for a member it does not hold, and `registryMemberServedAt` drops another package's member on its address. The pinned CONTROL (naming the base does not serve the dependent's addition; a third package is refused naming the base) matches the code.
- The nine other types: no change. `packageScopedHoldersOf` returns before it reads the caller when the type has no discriminator, and the keep is behind `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS[type] !== undefined`. Both are pinned per type.
- Change 2 (the pair keep): holds for the case it was written for (a pair's added locale on its base's address, #28802 ruling A); its edge is F2.
- "First-party callers 0" for the narrowed read: holds by reading. `StudioBundleItemEditor` reads at the package its list names the item under; `ResourceListPage` links a row at the row's own `_packageId`, and falls back to the active package only for an unstamped row, which a package-scoped list does not seat and the cross-package leg links with no package; `ResourceEditPage` reads at the URL's package. The send names none. No other reader under `packages/` or `ui/` names a package for an email template.

**Nits (prose faces only).**

- N1: the `Clause-②:` line does not name the bare `/meta/email_template/NAME` 409 for a clash sealed before phase 1 (ADR-0150, covered-types paragraph).
- N2: `bare-name-one-holder.ts` says the send "reads the resolved holder's bundle only"; the loader does not filter by the resolved holder, it relies on the layered list leaving a dependent's addition out, as `template-loader.ts` itself says. A doc sentence in code, so left as a follow-up, not a fix on this head.
- N3: the dev report's `dogfood_battery` line contradicts the PR title and arm (see ③).

No security item.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic rulings on the #32089 contract review (seat 1, F1 and F2).**

- **F1: agreed, and it is a root fix.** The send path resolves the template by D3 from the caller's package, with the flow `notify` node passing the flow's armed package (never the definition's stamps). A send with no package keeps the bare-name meaning: the environment item, else the one holder, else 409 naming every holder. Without this, flipping the switch would refuse every send of a two-holder name, which breaks "readers before narrowing".
- **F2: refuse both, when two pairs could own the row** (red line 2). X and Y both pair App A, and a Studio-added locale row on the pair carries no `overrides` and no binding. That row cannot say whether it is X's customization or Y's. Serving it to both `?package=X` and `?package=Y` gives one package's member to the other.
  - **Two or more pairs:** the exact qualifier answers 409 naming X and Y for that member, and `os migrate stored-references` lists the row so the operator can bind it.
  - **Exactly one pair:** it is served to that pair, as #28390 ruling A has it.
  - **The base's own address** (`?package=A`) keeps ruling A.
  - **Pins:** with two pairs, both exact reads of that member refuse with 409; with one pair, it is served; after a bind, only the bound pair is served.
- **A legacy package-less row read under two holders.** Today both exact addresses serve it, and main already does this for E8's nine types. That is the same defect class (D4: a package-less row is the customization of *one* holder, and with two holders it cannot say which). This PR declares it. No new card is filed while the maintainer's stop holds. It is recorded on #31527 as an open item, and it must be refused for every covered type before that type narrows.
